I need to figure out the secondary structure around V348, so I'm pulling the CA coordinates for residues 344-348 to compute backbone distances and check for helix or strand geometry.

Computing the pairwise distances, the 347-348 and 348-349 spacing look like standard consecutive CA distances around 3.8, but the 344-348 and 345-348 distances are too extended for a helix, suggesting this region is in an extended or coil conformation rather than helical.

This also reminds me that the sequence pattern with the paired cysteines looks like a nuclear receptor zinc-finger DNA-binding domain, which would fit with an extended, non-helical fold in this segment.

Continuing the sequence through residue 402, I notice this pattern with the two zinc-binding regions and the basic residue cluster near the end (KRKLIEENREKRRRE) strongly resembles a nuclear receptor DNA-binding domain, possibly from the thyroid hormone receptor family.

I'm checking whether the loop residues around 348-352 form part of a small antiparallel beta sheet, comparing to known short beta structures in glucocorticoid receptor DBDs, and calculating backbone N and O atom coordinates near valine 348 and cysteine 347 to test for hydrogen bonding with another strand.

Checking other nearby residues' CA distances from V348 but none seem close enough to be a real strand partner, so I'm not finding an obvious pairing in this region.

Looking for any hint of a helical turn instead, but the CA spacing across residues 346-350 is way too large for that, ruling out helix too.

Leaning toward classifying V348 as coil, though I want to verify there's no beta bridge by checking backbone atom distances (N, O) more closely before finalizing.

Checking that distance confirms it's too far for a hydrogen bond, so coil it is.
